from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Three rods, multiple disks.", "Never place larger on smaller.", "Goal: move the entire stack."]
        self.setup_layout("The Towers of Hanoi Rules", lecture_lines)
        
        # Load assets
        rod_img = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/peg.svg"
        disk_img = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg"
        
        rods = VGroup(*[SVGMobject(rod_img, color="#FF4500") for _ in range(3)])
        disks = VGroup(*[SVGMobject(disk_img) for _ in range(3)])
        labels = VGroup(*[Text(label, color="#FFD700", font_size=24) for label in ["A", "B", "C"]])
        
        # Position rods (B-row per Critic 25)
        self.place_at_grid(rods[0], 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(rods[1], 'B4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(rods[2], 'B6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Position labels (C-row per Critic 25/26)
        self.place_at_grid(labels[0], 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(labels[1], 'C4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(labels[2], 'C6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Position disks on rod A
        for i, disk in enumerate(disks):
            disk.scale(0.5 + i * 0.1)
            disk.move_to(rods[0].get_bottom() + UP * (0.1 + i * 0.3))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(RED), FadeIn(rods), FadeIn(labels), FadeIn(disks))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        moving_disk = disks[2].copy()
        self.play(moving_disk.animate.move_to(rods[2].get_bottom() + UP * 0.1))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(FadeOut(moving_disk))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Disk moves follow binary counts.",
            "The first '1' indicates the move.",
            "Binary numbers map to disk moves.",
            "Sequence links binary to disk actions.",
            "Patterns reveal the underlying logic."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Binary Connection", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        disk_asset = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Represent 3-disk solution as '111' in binary.
        binary_label = Text("Binary: 111", font_size=30, color=BLUE)
        disk = SVGMobject(disk_asset, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(binary_label, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(disk, "B3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(binary_label), FadeIn(disk))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate '111' becoming '7' in decimal.
        decimal_label = Text("Decimal: 7", font_size=30, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(decimal_label, "B6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Transform(binary_label.copy(), decimal_label))
        self.play(FadeIn(decimal_label))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw green (#32CD32) path connecting binary to disks
        path = Line(binary_label.get_right(), disk.get_left(), color="#32CD32")
        self.play(Create(path))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#32CD32")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Highlight disk movement sync with binary sequence.
        disk_move = Text("Move Disk", font_size=30, color=RED)
        self.place_in_area(disk_move, "E2", "E4", scale_factor=0.75)
        self.play(FadeIn(disk_move))
        self.lecture[3].set_color(RED)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Patterns reveal the underlying logic.
        logic_label = Text("Logic: 2^n - 1", font_size=24, color=PURPLE)
        self.place_at_grid(logic_label, "D5", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(logic_label))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(PURPLE)

        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Binary Logic in the Towers of Hanoi
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in computer science and discrete mathematics

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Nature of Binary
sections.content: Briefly introduce the binary system (base-2). Explain that just as decimal uses 0-9, binary uses 0 and 1 to represent powers of two. Focus on the concept of 'bit position' representing 2^n.
sections.example: Visualizing a 3-bit counter: 000 (0), 001 (1), 010 (2), 011 (3), 100 (4). Animation: As the binary number increments, a single bit flips at each step.

sections.title: The Towers of Hanoi Rules
sections.content: Define the classic puzzle: 3 rods, n disks of different sizes. Rule 1: Move one disk at a time. Rule 2: Never place a larger disk on a smaller one. Goal: Move the full tower to another rod.
sections.example: A 3-disk stack. An animation shows the illegal move (big disk on small) being blocked by a red 'X', while legal moves are highlighted in green.

sections.title: The Binary Connection
sections.content: Introduce the breakthrough insight: The sequence of disk moves follows the rhythm of a binary counter. In a 3-disk puzzle, the disk to move is determined by the position of the first '1' bit in the binary sequence of steps.
sections.example: Step 1 (001): Move Disk 1. Step 2 (010): Move Disk 2. Step 3 (011): Move Disk 1 again. Animation syncs binary numbers 1-7 on the left with disk movements on the right.

sections.title: Scaling to Complexity
sections.content: Explain why this works: The minimum number of moves is 2^n - 1. Connect this to the binary capacity of n bits. This shows that the puzzle is essentially a physical representation of an n-bit binary counter.
sections.example: A cute robot character attempting the puzzle. If the robot follows the 'binary instruction set' (even for 10 disks), it solves it perfectly without ever checking the rules.

sections.title: Summary & Application
sections.content: Wrap up by emphasizing that complex recursive problems can often be mapped to simple binary patterns. This is the foundation of how computers process logic.
sections.example: Display a final graphic: A 'Binary-Tower Cheat Sheet' where a scroll of paper with binary numbers 001, 010, 011... directly maps to the disk movement instructions.
